text: Mass media in Brittany serve the Breton language through journals, radio, and television. Breton journals appeared in the late nineteenth century. The three most important were Feiz ha Breiz, the weekly Kroaz ar Vretoned, and Dihunamb. They were written in dialect for a rural religious audience. The weekly Arvor ran from 1942 to 1944. Breton reached the radio waves in 1940 on Radio Roazon-Breiz, whose broadcasts continued through the German occupation. Radio-Kimerc'h resumed the service in 1946. Local private stations raised the hours of Breton broadcasts, and Radio Kreiz Breizh alone supplied twenty one hours a week. In 1998 Radio Kerne and Arvorig FM started and gave eighty percent of their air-time to Breton. Breton first reached television in 1964, though weekly air-time stayed short. TV Breizh launched in September 2000 as a privately funded cable and satellite channel. It was Europe's first bilingual regional generalist channel and carried programmes in both Breton and French.
